entry.title: Coinbase Agentic Wallets vs Agent Wallet SDK: What the Custody Difference Actually Means
entry.summary:
Coinbase launched Agentic Wallets a week ago. It's getting a lot of attention — and rightfully so. Giving AI agents a wallet is a fundamentally important primitive. I've been building a non-custodial alternative, so let me explain what's actually different and when each approach makes sense. Coinbase Agentic Wallets: Fast to set up, Coinbase holds the keys, requires Coinbase as infrastructure. Agent Wallet SDK: Takes 15 minutes to deploy, you hold the keys, runs on any EVM chain, no middleman. Coinbase built enterprise-grade infrastructure for agents to hold and spend USDC. It integrates natively with their x402 protocol, which I also support. Key features: Cloud Key Management System (KMS) — they store keys in HSMs Programmable spend limits Built-in compliance and KYC hooks Gas abstraction For teams that want to ship fast and already trust Coinbase, this is a strong choice. The tradeoff is lock-in: you can't self-host this, you can't move off Coinbase infrastructure, and you're trusting them with your agent's keys. Agent Wallet SDK is a non-custodial smart contract wallet on Base (ERC-6551 Token Bound Accounts + ERC-4337). The agent never holds keys — its permissions flow from an NFT that the human controls.
Scenario Use
Want to ship in an afternoon Coinbase
Enterprise with Coinbase relationship Coinbase
Need self-custody + no third-party risk Agent Wallet SDK
Want on-chain enforced spend limits Agent Wallet SDK
Coinbase model: Trust Coinbase's KMS. Our model: Trust the math. Spend limits are in the contract, code is audited and open. npm: npm install agentwallet-sdk
ClawHub: up2itnow/agentwallet-sdk
267 tests, 2 internal audits, Base Mainnet + Sepolia
